 Order

The challenge in this Crl.MC is against Annexure 8 order of the Additional Sessions Court-III,
Alappuzha, directing to release petitioner's vehicles on furnishing bank security of Rs.24,50,000/-.
2.

The short facts are as under;
The petitioner was an employee of an establishment by the name 'Nedumparambil Credit Syndicate'.

Based on complaints filed by the depositors of the establishment, crimes were registered alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of IPC as well as Sections 21 and 5 r/w Section 23 of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (BUDS Act).

entities.text: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (BUDS Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: During the course of the investigation of those crimes, the petitioner's Motor Cycle and Toyota Urban Cruiser car were seized by the Investigating Officer.

As the petitioner is not an accused in the crime under investigation, he approached 2025:KER:20830 the court below seeking release of the vehicle under Section 503 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and the impugned order was passed.

In view of the observation in the order that the vehicles were attached,
clarification was sought from the learned Additional Sessions Judge as to whether the impugned order is passed under Section 503 of BNSS or in accordance with the provisions of the BUDS Act.

In the report, the learned Judge has stated that even though the petition was filed under Section 503 of James Jacob vs State Of Kerala on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198464721/
2 BNSS the order is issued in accordance with the provisions of the BUDS Act.

entities.text: James Jacob vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Heard, learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
4. A reading of the impugned order makes it abundantly clear that the order is not issued by following the procedure prescribed under the BUDS Act.
On that sole ground the order is liable to be set aside.

Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that further delay will cause substantial prejudice to his client, since the vehicles are lying in the Police 2025:KER:20830 Station premises exposed to the vagaries of weather.

The Crl.MC is hence disposed of by quashing Annexure 8 order and directing the court below to reconsider the petitioner's application as one filed under the provisions of the BUDS Act and pass appropriate orders thereon within ten days of receipt of a copy of this order.
